title: A derivation not killing a non-p-th power
statement: Let $p$ be a prime number and let $B$ be an integral domain with $p\cdot1=0$ in $B$, with fraction field $L=B_{(0)}$ [def-weil-pbc-localization-at-prime]. Let $f\in B$ be an element which is not a $p$-th power in $L$. Assume that $B$ is a finitely generated algebra [def-weil-pbc-finite-type-algebra] over some Noetherian [def-weil-pbc-noetherian-ring] local ring $(R,\mathfrak m)$ which is $\mathfrak m$-adically complete [def-weil-pbc-adically-complete-ring] (via some ring map $R\to B$). Then there exists a derivation $D:B\to B$ (an additive map with $D(ab)=aD(b)+bD(a)$) with $D(f)\ne0$.
